modesty is prototypically characterized by a combination of humility, agreeableness, and introversion.

modesty is a multifaceted trait that centrally entails humble, shy, solicitude, and not boastfulness and peripherally honesty, likability, nonarrogance, attention avoidance, plainness, and graciousness.

the everyday conceptions that individuals hold about psychological phenomena, and it is the prototypicality of such conceptions that we seek to identify and characterize.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the everyday conceptions of psychological modesty are both broad and deep.
everyday conceptions of humility, modesty, and humility are not synonymous, and that modesty is not merely the absence of arrogance.
everyday conceptions of the psychological phenomenon modesty are not only well-defined but also well-circumscribed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
everyday conceptions of psychological phenomena are often more complex than their formal definitions suggest.

everyday conceptions of psychological phenomena are not necessarily as simple and straightforward as one may assume, and that they can be systematically studied to yield theoretically useful insights.
the psychological study of everyday conceptions of psychological phenomena can provide valuable insights into the nature of those phenomena.
